failures.title: Jeep ERC 3.6 Pentastar Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Oil cooler / filter housing failure - all ERC years
items.whatHappens: The combined oil cooler and oil filter housing is made of plastic. Repeated heat cycles make it brittle; cracks develop, leading to oil leaks that pool in the V of the engine and drip down the back. The leak can be oil, coolant, or both. Overtightening the oil filter cap during changes (spec is only 18 ft-lb) accelerates failure.
items.repairVsReplace: The housing itself can be replaced - many owners upgrade to an aftermarket aluminium housing (£300-£600) which eliminates the problem permanently. If the leak has been ignored and oil pressure has dropped, bearing damage may have occurred, requiring a full engine replacement.

items.title: Rocker arm and lifter failure - the "Pentastar Tick"
items.whatHappens: Faulty rocker arms and lifters cause a ticking noise (especially on cold start) that can progress to misfires, reduced power, and eventually camshaft damage if ignored. The failure appears more common on the right cylinder bank, suggesting an oil flow design issue.
items.repairVsReplace: Rocker arm and lifter replacement is a top-end job (£800-£1,500 at an independent). If left until the camshaft is damaged, costs rise significantly. Full engine replacement is rarely needed unless oil starvation has occurred.

items.title: Cylinder head issues - early 2011-2013 models
items.whatHappens: Early Pentastar engines (2011-2013) suffered from left-cylinder-head leakage causing misfires (codes P0300, P0302, P0304, P0306). FCA issued an extended-warranty bulletin covering many 2011-2013 applications.
items.repairVsReplace: Cylinder head replacement under warranty (where applicable) or at specialist cost (£1,500-£2,500). ERC-coded engines (2016+) are not affected by this specific early issue - but a 2022 campaign addressed a small number of 3.6 engines requiring left-side head replacement for misfire.

failures.goodYearsLine: The ERC (2016+) benefits from ongoing refinement; the early cylinder-head issues of 2011-2013 are not present, though the oil cooler housing remains a weak point across all years. 2022+ models still use the same plastic oil cooler design.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the ERC 3.6 Pentastar
variants.intro: The ERC is one of several codes in Chrysler's Pentastar V6 family. Unlike the earlier ERB (2011-2015) which had known cylinder-head issues, the ERC (2016+) benefits from ongoing production refinements including revised VVL hardware and updated ECU calibration. Where to find the engine code: - On the engine block - a stamped label on the front-left side of the V6 (looking from the front) - On the V5C registration document under "Engine number" - the ERC code appears in the first three characters - On the driver's door pillar or under-bonnet VIN/engine sticker - Via a VIN decoder - enter your full VIN online to confirm the factory engine code Common confusions: | Similar code | Difference | Link | |--------------|------------|------| | ERB | Earlier Pentastar (2011-2015); left-cylinder-head misfire issues more common | [ERB engine] | | EHB | 3.6L Pentastar variant with different calibration | [EHB engine] | | EHD | 3.6L Pentastar variant | [EHD engine] |

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement ERC 3.6 Pentastar - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used ERC can make sense for older Grand Cherokee or Wrangler examples where vehicle value doesn't justify a recon unit. However - insist on documented service history and evidence that the oil cooler housing has been replaced or isn't leaking. The "Pentastar Tick" (rocker arm noise) is a red flag on any used unit; walk away if you hear it on cold start.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper ERC recon addresses the oil cooler housing (often upgraded to aluminium), replaces rocker arms and lifters, checks timing chain health, and renews all gaskets and seals. This is the sweet spot for most UK owners - the failure-prone components are addressed, you get 12-24 months warranty, and cost is far below a new unit.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild of the ERC is rarely needed unless the engine has suffered oil starvation from an ignored cooler leak, leading to bottom-end damage. If rebuilding, specify upgraded aluminium oil cooler housing, new timing chain and guides, and full rocker/lifter replacement. This is the "zero-risk" option for high-value Wrangler Rubicon or Grand Cherokee Overland examples.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Fitting through our network of vetted UK Jeep specialists - supply-only or full supply and fit, with nationwide delivery and warranty cover on every reconditioned and rebuilt unit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The ERC sits in vehicles with wide value ranges - a 2016 Grand Cherokee may be worth £8,000-£12,000, while a 2023 Wrangler Rubicon can exceed £40,000. For lower-value examples (sub-£8,000), a used engine with documented history may be the most financially sensible route. For higher-value or off-road-use vehicles, a reconditioned unit with upgraded oil cooler is the better long-term investment. Always evaluate the specific vehicle's condition and value before committing to a £4,000+ replacement.

faq.title: Jeep ERC 3.6 Pentastar - Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: What is the Jeep ERC 3.6 Pentastar engine replacement cost in the UK?
items.answer: A reconditioned ERC engine typically costs £2,800-£4,800 supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £3,600-£5,800 at an independent specialist. Used engines are cheaper at £1,500-£2,800 but carry higher risk. Rebuilt units go up to £6,500 supply-only. Labour adds 8-12 hours at £65-£85/hr.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the Jeep ERC Pentastar engine?
items.answer: The most common failure is the plastic oil cooler / filter housing, which cracks and leaks oil or coolant into the V of the engine. Typical onset is 40,000-100,000 miles. The fix is housing replacement; many owners upgrade to an aluminium unit (£300-£600) to prevent recurrence. If ignored, oil pressure drops can cause bottom-end bearing failure, requiring a full engine replacement.
bullets: The fix is housing replacement; many owners upgrade to an aluminium unit (£300-£600) to prevent recurrence.
If ignored, oil pressure drops can cause bottom-end bearing failure, requiring a full engine replacement.

items.question: Which Jeep models use the ERC 3.6 Pentastar engine?
items.answer: The ERC is fitted to core Jeep models from 2016 onward, including Grand Cherokee (WK2 2016-2022, WL 2021-present), Wrangler (JL 2017-present), and Gladiator (JT 2019-present).

items.question: What is the "Pentastar Tick" on the Jeep ERC engine?
items.answer: The Pentastar Tick is a tapping noise caused by failing rocker arms and lifters, most noticeable on cold start. Typical onset is 60,000-120,000 miles. It can progress to misfires and camshaft damage if ignored. Top-end repair costs £800-£1,500; full engine replacement is rarely needed unless oil starvation occurs.
bullets: It can progress to misfires and camshaft damage if ignored.
Top-end repair costs £800-£1,500; full engine replacement is rarely needed unless oil starvation occurs.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned ERC engine?
items.answer: Choose a used ERC only if it has full documented service history and the oil cooler has been replaced - otherwise, the risk of the same failures recurring is high. A reconditioned unit is the better choice for most owners, as it addresses the oil cooler (often upgraded to aluminium), replaces rocker arms and lifters, and includes a 12-24 month warranty. Browse reconditioned ERC engines with warranty.

items.question: How do I confirm my Jeep has the ERC engine code?
items.answer: Check three places: the engine block itself (a stamped label on the front-left side), your V5C registration document under "Engine number" (the first three characters are "ERC"), and use a VIN decoder online with your full 17-digit VIN to pull the factory build sheet.
